label: input token h during the original phase
explanation: Token detector for the letter h as an original (pre-<DEL>) input. Fires on essentially every original-phase step whose input is h (dev precision 1.0, recall 0.99, mass recall 0.997), at any position and for any sequence length. Activation is fairly uniform (mean 0.55, max 0.72). In the profile examples the strongest activations are on h late in long sequences and the weakest are on h early in shorter ones, but I only saw this in examples and did not measure it. It does not fire on h when h is fed back as input during the copy phase (only ~1300 copy-phase activations, mostly at recall_idx 1), never at the <DEL> step, and essentially never on other tokens (63 weak hits on d).

issues: The hedged magnitude claim is wrong. Activation mass divided by active count, by orig_idx, comes out to about 1.11e-5 at position 0, about 0.85e-5 at positions 2-4 and about 0.95e-5 at positions 7-8. So the strongest activations are on h at position 0, not late in long sequences. By L the values are flat (about 0.98e-5 at L=3 vs 0.92e-5 at L=9). The misses examples agree: the top activations (0.93 relative to max) are h at orig_idx 0. The sentence should be removed or reversed.

The core predicate holds on the test split: precision 1.000, recall 0.988, no false positives. The missed activations (1344 steps, 0.3% of mass) are almost all weak copy-phase h at recall_idx 1, and the examples are sequences that start with h. That is a small, explainable tail, not a counterexample class. (phase==2)&(in_tok==h) scores precision 0.014, and all of its coverage is in the bottom activation quartile.
The d hits are negligible as claimed: in_tok==d gives 64 active steps on test, all in the bottom quartile.
Adding copy-phase h at recall_idx 1 raises recall to 0.999 but drops precision to 0.877 (F1 0.934), so the original predicate is the better one.
